subject: Accounting for misreported and/or under reported count data

messages.author: b431df4437cb4a5f
messages.subject: Accounting for misreported and/or under reported count data
parts:
Recently are referee on a manuscript suggested that we account for misreported or under reported count data in our model. The model we use is a negative binomial spec for the counts themselves and the typical random effects for a BYM2, RW1, Type 1 spatial temporal interaction. One paper was suggested which seems to follow a Poisson - Logistic pogit framework.  Full article: A Hierarchical Framework for Correcting Under-Reporting in Count Data (tandfonline.com).

However, I am not sure how I would set this up in the INLA formula. I do not believe there to be a built in function for this like there is with the ZIP and ZINB models.

Below is my formula pasted. Any help on how to set this up would be much appreciated.

formula_All_ThruOct21.int1<- Cases ~ 1 + scaledSVI + scaledSOVI + scaledNRI + scaledBRIC + scaledTemp + scaledPrecip +
  f(ID.area,model="bym2", graph=H, hyper = bym2prior) +
  f(ID.month,model="rw1", scale.model = TRUE) + f(ID.month1,model="iid") + f(ID.area.month,model="iid")

modCases_ThruOct21_linked.intI <- inla(formula_All_ThruOct21.int1,family="nbinomial",data=dataAllWithDiscrete, E=ExpectedCases,
                                   control.predictor=list(link=1),
                                   control.compute=list(openmp.strategy="pardiso.parallel",dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE), verbos = TRUE)

parts:
I had a quick look at the paper, and I do not think you're able to run
it in INLA (conditionally, you can, but that is a different issue).

when the true 'y' is (partly) missing, then it needs to be integrated
out, and that is where the problem is.

Best
H
